requirement: Implement an audit dispatch verifier AuditDispatchVerifier that tests an event notifier. Must use exact, valid Mock assertion methods (assert_called_once_with, call_count == 1). Must never use non-existent methods (like assert_not_called_with) or uninvoked attribute accesses (mock.assert_called_once without parentheses).
skeleton: An event dispatcher EventDispatcher and verifier function verify_single_dispatch(sink, expected_event, expected_payload).
caption: A standard-library event dispatcher and verifier built on unittest.mock that uses real Mock assertion methods, called with parentheses, to prove exactly one dispatch with the expected arguments, with no third-party imports. EventDispatcher stores a sink and its dispatch(event_name, payload) calls the sink with the event name and payload. verify_single_dispatch(sink, expected_event, expected_payload) calls sink.assert_called_once_with with the expected event and payload, which fails on zero calls, on more than one call, and on mismatched arguments; it then separately checks that call_count is exactly one and raises AssertionError reporting the actual count otherwise, and returns True. It avoids misspelled assertion names that do not exist on Mock, which merely return a child mock and assert nothing, avoids referencing an assertion method without calling it, and avoids assert_called_with, which inspects only the most recent call. The fixture asserts that one dispatch of order_placed with order_id 42 and amount 99.5 verifies as True, that a mismatched payload raises AssertionError, that dispatching the same event twice raises AssertionError, that a sink that was never called raises AssertionError, that a single valid call still returns True, and that a triple dispatch raises AssertionError.

rationale.teaches: A verifier that calls assert_called_once_with with parentheses and the expected arguments, and checks call_count equals exactly one.
rationale.why: A misspelled Mock assertion returns a new child mock instead of asserting, and an un-called method reference does nothing, so a broken verifier passes every test. The fixture dispatches twice and zero times and expects the verifier to fail.

candidates.why_wrong: assert_not_called_with does not exist on Mock, so the call returns a child mock and asserts nothing.
assert_called_with checks only the last call and the count check allows more than one, so a double dispatch passes.
assert_called_once is referenced without parentheses and the count check is never false, so nothing is verified.
The count check is inverted, so exactly one call fails and any other count passes.
The count check only fails above two, so zero or two dispatches pass.
